perseid meteor shower 2026: it’s time to watch

12k views · 108 reactions | on august 12, 2026, skywatchers across parts of the northern hemisphere will witness one of the most spectacular astronomical events in years. a total solar eclipse will cross greenland, iceland, spain, and parts of portugal, while many other regions will experience a partial eclipse. around the same period, six planets—mercury, venus, jupiter, saturn, uranus, and neptune—will be visible in the sky under favorable conditions, and the perseid meteor shower will be near its annual peak, producing up to 50–100 meteors per hour under dark skies.

the perseids are created as earth passes through debris left behind by comet swift–tuttle, with meteors entering earth's atmosphere at speeds of about 59 km/s (133,000 mph). although not every location will see all three phenomena simultaneously because of daylight, geography, and planet visibility, the convergence of these major celestial events makes august 2026 one of the most remarkable months for astronomy enthusiasts in recent years.

source: nasa / esa / international astronomical union, 2026
